commit_date_range.latest_on_main_source_command: git log -1 main --format='%cI' | python3 -c "import sys; from datetime import datetime, timezone; print(datetime.fromisoformat(sys.stdin.read().strip()).astimezone(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'))"
commit_date_range.earliest_aliases_note: 'earliest' and 'earliest_utc' carry the identical value. The '_utc' suffix variant is the CP2-contract field name; the unsuffixed variant is preserved as a compatibility alias for consumers and the JSON schema's required-field list. The same applies to 'latest' / 'latest_utc'. 'latest_on_main' is a new CP2-contract field that records the HEAD-on-default-branch committer timestamp in UTC, distinct from 'latest' which spans --all refs and may include feature-branch commits beyond main.
commit_date_range.latest_vs_latest_on_main_note: 'latest' = 2026-05-21T19:48:23Z is the latest commit reachable from any branch in the repository (the source command 'git log --all --format=%aI | sort -r | head -1' across refs/heads/ and refs/remotes/origin/ feature branches). 'latest_on_main' = 2026-05-15T21:00:51Z is the HEAD committer timestamp of main only ('git log -1 main --format=%cI' normalised to UTC). The 6.1-day gap reflects feature-branch activity on blitzy-* branches after the most recent main merge.
